properties.abstract: Exploring the home of Tête de Moine: This athletically challenging stage starts and ends in Bellelay, with its well-known abbey, where the famous cheese is said to have first been made. Climbs and descents alternate during the subsequent tour through the Petit-Val. There are stunning views across the Jura mountains along the way.
properties.description:
As the birthplace of the famous Tête de Moine speciality cheese, Bellelay has a lot to offer: for example, a visit to the historic cheese dairy, a tour of the baroque-style abbey or a stop at the historic Hôtel de l’Ours. The physically demanding bike tour begins right away with an initial climb through the forest to the next fold of the Jura. A short, fast-paced descent then ends in Fornet-Dessous. Tête de Moine is also made in one of the cheese dairies here. What makes this cheese special is that it isn’t sliced, but shaved into decorative rosettes using a special tool called a girolle.

The stretch now winds up and down through the hilly landscape and small hamlets. Steep, unsurfaced trails connect Rebévelier to the next fold of the Jura. Once you reach the top, you have a sweeping view of the impressive Jura mountains in the north. The subsequent fast-paced descent across a slope ends in the idyllically located hamlet of Châtelat in the basin of the upper Sorne valley. The name of the municipality of Petit-Val says it all: The many small valleys give this tour its special character. 

The forest trail up to Moron is steep, rugged and narrow in places. In the hamlet of the same name, a board gives information on the surrounding area. You now make two further descents and one climb up to the Montagne de Saules. A stony, sometimes steep track takes you up to the highest point of the tour: the Bergerie de Loveresse, where there is a restaurant. The peak of the Moron, with the striking tower designed by world-renowned architect Mario Botta, is only around three kilometres away. 

The next section of the route doesn’t lead up to the peak, but steeply downwards through the forest. The bumpy mountain road ends in the village of Loveresse in the Vallée de Tavannes. From here, you take a leisurely ride westwards, along the foot of the hill, before it gets more challenging again: The final climb, on trails and across typical Jura meadows, ends on a high plateau. You cycle around the extensive moorland of La Sagne and finally end the tour back at the starting point in Bellelay.
properties.title: Bellelay Bike
